html:
The Kingdom of Antigonus was the realm of Antigonus I Monophthalmus, "the One-Eyed", one of the generals of Alexander the Great. At its height it held Anatolia and Syria, as this map shows around 300 BCE.

After Alexander's death in 323 BCE, Antigonus held Phrygia in Anatolia. In the wars of the successors he became the strongest of them and tried to rebuild the whole empire under his own rule. In 306 BCE he and his son Demetrius Poliorcetes took the title of king.

His rivals united against him. In 301 BCE Lysimachus and Seleucus, with war elephants from India, defeated and killed Antigonus, then over 80, at the Battle of Ipsus. His lands were shared out, much of Syria going to the Seleucid Empire. Demetrius survived, and his descendants, the Antigonid dynasty, later ruled Macedon until Rome conquered it in 168 BCE.
